question: What is the primary material applied directly to a wound to protect it called?
explanation: A wound dressing is the sterile material placed directly on a wound to protect it and aid healing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is keeping a wound at the right moisture level so important?

options.A: It completely stops all forms of bleeding
options.B: It promotes tissue repair and prevents dehydration
options.C: It eliminates the need for antiseptic solutions
options.D: It prevents the dressing from sticking permanently

explanation: Great job! Keeping the wound nicely hydrated helps new skin cells move in and speeds up the whole healing process. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: What do we call a wound that gets stuck and fails to go through the normal healing stages smoothly?
explanation: Spot on! Chronic wounds stall out in the inflammatory stage, often because of other health challenges the patient might have. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: How would you classify a wound that already has dead tissue and an active infection?
explanation: You've got it! Wounds with germs, foreign bits, or dead tissue right from the start are classed as dirty or infected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which dressing turns into a soft gel when it soaks up heavy fluid from a wound?
explanation: Well done! Alginate dressings are champs at drinking up heavy drainage and turning into a soothing gel. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: A patient has a shallow leg ulcer with very little drainage. Which dressing is best to use?
explanation: Correct! Hydrocolloids create a nice, moist home for shallow wounds that don't leak too much fluid. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: When cleaning a wound during a dressing change, what is the safest direction to wipe?

options.A: Randomly across the entire surface of the open skin
options.B: From the least contaminated area to the most contaminated area
options.C: From the most contaminated area toward the healthy skin
options.D: From the outside edges straight into the deep center

explanation: You're right! Always clean from the cleanest part toward the dirtier parts so you don't push germs back into the wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why do nurses strictly use aseptic technique when changing dressings?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any antibiotic medications
options.B: To speed up the patient's physical mobility recovery
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To prevent introducing microorganisms and causing infection

explanation: Spot on! Keeping things sterile stops hospital germs from crashing the party and causing a new infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: During a dressing change, when should you take off your dirty gloves and put on a fresh pair?

options.A: After removing the old dressing and before inspecting the wound
options.B: Only after the entire new dressing has been completely taped
options.C: Right after opening the sterile packaging supplies on the tray
options.D: Before washing hands at the start of the clinical procedure

explanation: Well reasoned! Take off the gloves used for the dirty old dressing, clean your hands, and use a fresh pair to keep things clean. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why should you take a close look at the old dressing after taking it off?

options.A: To test the tensile strength of the adhesive tape used
options.B: To evaluate the amount, color, and odor of wound drainage
options.C: To determine if the doctor made a mistake in the medication
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital materials

explanation: You've got it! The old dressing tells a story—its drainage gives you huge clues about how well the wound is healing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which of these details is NOT needed when charting a wound dressing change?

options.A: The size and depth measurements of the open wound
options.B: The type of sterile dressing material applied afterward
options.C: The brand name of the soap the patient used at home
options.D: The appearance and color of any drainage on the pad

explanation: Correct! What soap the patient uses at home isn't part of your clinical dressing change notes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h6)

question: Why do we regularly document wound healing progress in the nursing notes?

options.A: To prove that the nurse worked the full shift hours
options.B: To track progress and detect signs of complications early
options.C: To satisfy administrative paperwork quotas without clinical value
options.D: To replace the need for physical assessments by physicians

explanation: Spot on! Good charting helps the whole healthcare team catch any trouble early and make sure the wound keeps healing nicely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h6)
